channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio cola em Lula entre mais jovens, mas petista se mantém à frente no 1º turno em todas as faixas etárias
item.description: Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) gaining 6 percentage points among 16-24 year olds, narrowing the gap with Lula (PT), who still leads numerically across all age groups in the first round. In a simulated second round, Lula leads with 47% against Flávio's 45%. Despite the negative shift among youth, Lula advanced in the 25-35 and 45-59 age brackets.

item.title: ACM Neto e Jerônimo empatam no 2º turno na Bahia, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 24, 2026 shows a technical tie between ACM Neto (União Brasil) and Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) in the 2nd round of the Bahia gubernatorial race, with 45% and 43% respectively. In the 1st round data, Neto leads with 42% followed by Jerônimo with 40%. The survey also indicates a tie between Rui Costa and Jaques Wagner (both PT) in the Senate race.

item.title: Zanin pede que Anatel se manifeste em ação que pede internet móvel livre no período eleitoral
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Cristiano Zanin ordered Anatel, AGU, and PGR to provide input on a lawsuit seeking unrestricted mobile internet access during the election period. The Green Party and CNTE allege Anatel's omission in not regulating internet access after data quotas are exhausted. Zanin set a 48-hour deadline for responses while keeping the case under review.

item.title: Lula vence em todos os cenários na Bahia, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 25, 2026 shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading with 58% of voting intentions in Bahia, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 23%. In a simulated second round, Lula maintains an edge with 62% against Flávio's 27%. The survey interviewed 900 voters between September 20 and 23, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Datafolha: como os colunistas do GLOBO analisaram a nova pesquisa que traz Lula com 40% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 36%, no 1º turno
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows Lula leading with 40% in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 36%. In the second round, Lula is at 47% against Flávio's 45%. Both candidates have high rejection rates (45%).

item.title: Quaest: como está a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro em BA, SE, RS, SC, GO, AM, RO e AP
item.description: The Quaest polls released on September 24, 2026 show Lula (PT) leading over Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) across the eight surveyed regions. In Bahia and Sergipe, Lula holds large leads, while in Goiás the race is tighter with strong performance by Ronaldo Caiado (PSD). The surveys were conducted between September 20-23 with a 3-point margin of error.

item.title: Em Minas, Flávio Bolsonaro agradece Nikolas: “Apoio para mudar o Brasil”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro publicly thanked federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira, reaffirming his support for the presidential campaign base in Brasília. The statement comes amid internal tensions within the Bolsonarist camp, with Nikolas seeking to reinforce his role in the campaign. Flávio also backed Flávio Roscoe for governor of Minas Gerais, emphasizing policies for attracting investments.

item.title: Rogério Correia pede ao STF investigação sobre voo de Flávio com Willer Tomaz
item.description: Federal deputy Rogério Correia (PT-MG) filed a lawsuit with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) requesting an investigation into a trip taken by senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), relatives, and lawyer Willer Tomaz aboard an executive jet allegedly linked to former banker Daniel Vorcaro. The motion asks the Federal Police to investigate potential irregularities in the aircraft's acquisition or usage.

item.title: Quaest aponta empate técnico entre cinco candidatos ao Senado no RS
item.description: A Quaest poll shows a technical tie among five candidates for the two Senate seats in Rio Grande do Sul, within a 3-point margin of error. Manuela d'Ávila leads with 14%, followed by Marcel van Hattem (11%), Paulo Pimenta and Ubiratan Sanderson (10%), and Germano Rigotto (9%). 30% of voters remain undecided.

item.title: Em bloquinho com Nikolas, Flávio manda "triste recado ao sistema podre"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro spoke in Teófilo Otoni, promising to be sworn in by his father Jair Bolsonaro and declaring war on drug trafficking. He criticized the political system and reinforced the Bolsonaro movement's candidacy.

item.title: Ofensiva miliciana
item.description: The CartaCapital editorial highlights the militia offensive in the 2026 election scenario, with leaked messages from Daniel Vorcaro revealing ties to the Bolsonaro clan and funding for Jair Bolsonaro's biopic. The campaign is marked by unstable polls and debate shifts toward the STF crisis, while sovereignty and institutional survival gain relevance in the final stretch.

item.title: Raquel Lyra usa Boulos na TV como munição contra João Campos
item.description: Raquel Lyra used Guilherme Boulos in campaign ads to criticize João Campos, highlighting contradictions in the Pernambuco politician's stance toward the PT and Lula. The ad references 2020 comments by Campos on PT corruption and recent remarks by Boulos about Campos' political shift. The move coincides with Lula's visit to Pernambuco during the final stretch of the first round.

item.title: Governo federal manda derrubar 1,3 mil contas que divulgam bets irregulares
item.description: The federal government removed 1,367 social media accounts promoting irregular betting platforms, as part of a joint operation by the Ministry of Justice and the Cyber Operations Laboratory. At the same time, President Lula will sign a provisional decree tightening regulations for online betting platforms, accompanied by bill proposals to Congress that increase penalties and criminalize new forms of illegal betting.

item.title: Barrado pelo TSE, Arruda chama momento de “última missão” no DF
item.description: Former Federal District governor José Roberto Arruda had his Palace of Justice candidacy blocked by the TSE and chose not to appeal, calling it his 'last mission.' His ineligibility is tied to judicial convictions with a minimum eight-year ban that would not expire before the October elections.

item.title: Quem tem poder escolhe o relator do próprio caso no Brasil; é a morte do juiz natural
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) carried out a legal maneuver to prevent Minister André Mendonça from being the rapporteur of an action that could harm Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), requesting Minister Flávio Dino to rule on a different topic from the original case. Columnist Carlos Andreazza criticizes this practice, calling it the 'killed death of natural justice,' noting that whoever holds political power ends up choosing the judge who will hear their case.

item.title: Para além da inconveniência: distorções informacionais nas eleições
item.description: A study by UK-based organization Eko revealed that Instagram accepted political ads paid for in the United States containing false information targeted at the Brazilian public. The news, published by Folha on September 24, 2026, highlights information distortions that could impact the 2026 election.

item.title: Omar Aziz lidera corrida pelo governo do Amazonas, aponta Quaest
item.description: Senator Omar Aziz (PSD) leads the race for Amazonas governor with 29% of voting intentions, followed by Professor Maria do Carmo (PL) with 19%. The Quaest poll released on Thursday also shows Roberto Cidade (União Brasil) with 18% and David Almeida (Avante) with 11%.

item.title: Quaest: Dr. Furlan lidera disputa no Amapá com 53%, ante 40% de Clécio Luís
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 24, 2026 shows former Macapá mayor Dr. Furlan (PSD) leading the race for Amapá governor with 53% of first-round voting intentions, ahead of incumbent Clécio Luís (União Brasil) at 40%.

item.title: Quaest aponta empate técnico entre ACM Neto e Jerônimo na Bahia
item.description: The Quaest poll, commissioned by TV Bahia and conducted between September 20 and 23 with 900 voters, shows a technical tie between ACM Neto (União Brasil) at 42% and Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) at 40% in the race for Bahia governor. In a hypothetical runoff, Neto leads with 45% against 43% for the incumbent. The margin of error is three percentage points.

item.title: Roubo ou queima de arquivo?
item.description: Milton Leite's office was robbed after his arrest for links to PCC. Meta censored comedian Fábio Porchat's content about the Lagoinha scandal. Eduardo Bolsonaro was dismissed from the Federal Police for abandoning his post.

item.title: Quaest em RO: Flávio Bolsonaro, 53%; Lula, 19%; Augusto Cury, 4%; Ronaldo Caiado, 3%; Renan Santos, 2%
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads the Quaest poll in Rondônia with 53%, followed by Lula with 19%. The survey, commissioned by Rede Amazônica, interviewed 804 voters from September 20-23 with a 3-point margin of error.

item.title: Quaest: Daniel Vilela segue na liderança da disputa ao Governo de Goiás
item.description: Quaest poll released on September 24, 2026 confirms Daniel Vilela (MDB) leading the race for Goiás Governor. He took office in March 2026 following Ronaldo Caiado's resignation (PSD).

item.title: Datafolha: 23% não sabem o número da urna do candidato a presidente em quem pretendem votar
item.description: A Datafolha survey reveals that 23% of voters do not know the electronic ballot number of the presidential candidate they intend to vote for, while 73% answer correctly and 3% cite the wrong number. Among Lula voters, 87% know the correct number, compared to 79% of those who support Flávio Bolsonaro, according to polling conducted with 2,002 people on September 22 and 23.

item.title: Quaest em SE: 68% aprovam e 24% desaprovam governo de Fábio
item.description: A Quaest survey in Sergipe shows that 68% of respondents approve of Governor Fábio Mitidieri's administration, while 24% disapprove. The main concerns among voters are health (27%) and the water crisis (24%).

item.title: O fim da química
item.description: At the UN General Assembly opening, Lula and Trump displayed mutual hostility, with U.S. representatives refusing to applaud the Brazilian president's speech, in which he criticized North American interference in Latin America and Brazilian elections. The cold atmosphere contrasts with their friendly meeting the previous year, despite existing trade sanctions.

item.title: Datafolha: Tarcísio tem 50%, contra 30% de Haddad, e poderia vencer em 1º turno em SP
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas leads the São Paulo re-election race with 50% of total vote intentions, against Fernando Haddad on 30%, according to Datafolha. The poll indicates that the governor could win in the first round.

item.title: Ao vivo: PoderDataCast discute papel do TSE a 10 dias da eleição
item.description: PoderDataCast airs live on Thursday, Sept. 24, at 6:30 p.m., ten days before the first round, with former TSE minister Edilene Lôbo discussing voting machines, oversight, digital rules, and disinformation. The program will also analyze recent PoderData/Aya polling.

item.title: Brasil 'dá as costas ao futuro' em eleição com candidatos 'desoladores', diz The Economist
item.description: In an editorial on Brazil's 2026 election, The Economist sees little hope in a contest dominated by Lula and the Bolsonaro family. The magazine criticizes entrenched corruption and rising public spending while identifying Mission Party candidate Renan Santos as the outsider closest to what it believes the moment requires.

item.title: Fazenda vê elo entre verba de Dark Horse e estrutura usada pelo crime
item.description: Brazil's Minister of Finance, Dário Durigan, stated that funds used abroad to finance the film 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro show signs of circulating through the same financial structure used by criminal organizations investigated in Brazil. The statement was made during the third phase of Operation Carbon, highlighting potential links between production funding and criminal activities.

item.title: Defesa de Flávio pede a Fachin suspensão de pedidos de investigação no STF
item.description: The defense team of senator Flávio Bolsonaro requested Supreme Court Justice Edson Fachin to suspend ongoing investigations and investigation requests at the STF, arguing that the procedural flow would allow parties to indirectly choose the judge handling the case. The lawyers classify the practice as forum shopping, which they claim constitutes a legal flaw warranting nullity. The request was filed after investigations involving the senator were distributed among different STF justices.

item.title: Eleitores têm até 3 de outubro para baixar e validar e-Título
item.description: The TSE says voters must download and validate the e-Título by October 3, 2026, the day before the first round of Brazil’s general elections. The digital title is valid only when displayed online on a phone or tablet, not as a screenshot, and registration restrictions still prevent voting.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Os depósitos em dinheiro vivo para o guloso do Lulinha
item.description: Papo Antagonista discussed messages on Roberta Luchsinger's phone indicating coordination of cash payments to Lulinha, son of President Lula. Also covered the Provisional Measure banning online sports betting in Brazil.

item.title: Stuhlberger prevê alta de 30% da bolsa com vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Luis Stuhlberger predicts a 30% stock market rally if Flávio Bolsonaro wins, assigning 60% chance of victory to the candidate. He highlights low investor positioning and skepticism about structural reforms.

item.title: Zema sobre Alcolumbre e CPI do Master: "Se não fizer por bem, vai por mal"
item.description: Romeu Zema accused Davi Alcolumbre of blocking the Master Bank inquiry because, he said, he is involved with Daniel Vorcaro and called for a new Senate leader. Novo says it has gathered enough signatures for the inquiry and filed an ethics complaint against Alcolumbre over institutional inaction.

item.title: TSE diz à Procuradoria que chatbots de IA têm apresentado 'comportamento extremamente responsável'
item.description: The TSE informed the General Electoral Prosecutor's Office that generative AI chatbots have demonstrated responsible behavior. The models warn users that they cannot provide electoral recommendations or suggestions, in compliance with current regulations.

item.title: CARTUM: 1432
item.description: The CARTUM 1432 cartoon, published on the eve of the 2026 elections, warns that Brazil's democratic future is at stake again. The text notes the Bolsonarist threat has only retreated, not been defeated, while conservative forces set the pace in Congress and global instability worsens.

item.title: PT prepara “festa do interior” para visita de Lula à Bahia
item.description: President Lula (PT) is preparing a 'countryside celebration' during his visit to Bahia, stopping in Feira de Santana where he will hold a rally and deliver a speech. The campaign aims to mobilize his base in the state's interior with support from mayors and local leaders. The trip is part of the final stretch before the first round of the October 4th elections.

item.title: “Não votem mais em mim”, diz Arruda após decisão do TSE
item.description: Former governor José Roberto Arruda (PSD) will not appeal the TSE’s suspension of his candidacy for governor of the Federal District. Even if his name remains on the ballot, he asked voters not to vote for him.

item.title: Advogados deixam revisão criminal de Bolsonaro após desistência do pedido de liberdade
item.description: Bolsonaro's lawyers withdrew the habeas corpus request in his criminal review case at the Supreme Court after previously asking for his arrest to be suspended. The defense was taken over by Luciana Lauria Lopes, citing a strategic reassessment.

item.title: Ricardo Nunes minimiza fala de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre ida do prefeito a hospital veterinário
item.description: São Paulo mayor Ricardo Nunes downplayed a comment by senator Flávio Bolsonaro suggesting he could be treated at a new municipal veterinary hospital, saying he interpreted it as praise for the quality of animal care services. The remark was made during a campaign livestream with Governor Tarcísio de Freitas while discussing the hospital’s launch in São Paulo’s east zone. Nunes, who serves as Flávio’s electoral officer in São Paulo, emphasized the comment was not meant to be derogatory.

item.title: Delegação brasileira se retira do plenário da ONU durante discurso de Netanyahu
item.description: The Brazilian delegation withdrew from the UN General Assembly plenary during Benjamin Netanyahu's speech, expressing repudiation against Israel's actions. Other countries also left, as Netanyahu accused those present of moral cowardice. Brazil maintains a critical stance toward Israeli military operations in Gaza and supports the two-state solution.

item.title: Em carta a Rubio, 31 congressistas dos EUA acusam governo Trump de tentar interferir na eleição no Brasil
item.description: Thirty U.S. lawmakers wrote to Marco Rubio accusing the Trump administration of using tariffs, sanctions, and diplomatic pressure on Brazilian institutions during the legal proceedings against Jair Bolsonaro. The lawmakers condemned the alleged interference and called on Washington to accept the results of Brazil's October presidential election.

item.title: Marinho chama Messias de “militante do PT” após post sobre “Dark Horse”
item.description: Rogério Marinho called Justice Legal Affairs chief Jorge Messias a “PT activist” after he linked Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro to the Banco Master case and the financing of the film Dark Horse. Marinho accused Messias of using state institutions for the PT, while the attorney general demanded answers about the funds under investigation.

item.title: Associações lançam manifesto contra proibição das bets
item.description: Betting associations launched a manifesto against prohibition, warning of illegal market risks, mass layoffs, and legal uncertainty. They defend regulation under Law 14.790/2023 and call for dialogue instead of electoral disputes.

item.title: Crusoé: A relação de amor e ódio entre Lulinha e Roberta
item.description: The report describes an ambiguous relationship between lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger and Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha). She boasted of proximity to the president's son but showed impatience and irritation with him in private conversations.

item.title: Jovem nadador mira cenário nacional e sonha com Seleção Brasileira
item.description: Samuel Caldeira Costa Peron, 13, is a swimmer from Natação São Caetano who competed in the 2026 Brazilian Infant Winter Championship, placing seventh in the 200m breaststroke final. With ambitious goals, he aims for national titles, time improvements, and eventually the Brazilian National Team and Olympic Games.

item.title: Saiba até quando baixar o e-Título para usar o celular na votação
item.description: The TSE announces the deadline to download the e-Título app before the 2026 elections. Voters must download and access the app in advance to use their phone during voting in the first round. Access the e-Título regularly to avoid issues on election day.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não só ligou, mas implorou que Vorcaro o atendesse
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro allegedly called and begged Vorcaro to answer, reflecting a moment of political desperation. The incident highlights internal tensions in the 2026 Brazilian electoral landscape.

item.title: Lula endurece discurso sobre bets; Flávio critica regulamentação atual, mas defende aposta esportiva
item.description: Lula hardened his stance on online betting, promising to end sports gambling in the 2026 campaign, after previously stating in 2024 he would test regulations before banning. Flávio Bolsonaro criticizes online casinos but supports keeping sports betting under regulatory control.

item.title: Cury diz que Lula “destruirá” Flávio no 2º turno
item.description: Augusto Cury claimed Lula would defeat Flávio Bolsonaro in a runoff and stated he prefers facing him directly, denying any alliance. He criticized both candidates' political models and highlighted his own governance plan. In the polls, Cury has low support while Lula and Flávio lead the vote intentions.
